    if "consumer" not in params:
        raise ValueError("consumer is required")
    cursor = params.get("cursor")
    if cursor is not None and not all("0" <= char <= "9" for char in cursor):
        raise ValueError("cursor must be a decimal non-negative integer")
    limit = params.get("limit")
    if limit is not None:
        if not all("0" <= char <= "9" for char in limit):
            raise ValueError("limit must be a decimal integer")
        if not 1 <= int(limit) <= _MAX_LIMIT:
            raise ValueError("limit must be between 1 and 1000")
    return params


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "CarbonMarket/0.1"

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - BaseHTTPRequestHandler contract
        if self.path == "/health":
            self._json(HTTPStatus.OK, {"status": "ok"})
            return
        path, _, query = self.path.partition("?")
        if path == "/audit" \
                and getattr(self.server, "audit_path", None) is not None:
            self._audit(query)
            return
        if path == "/audit/proof" \
                and getattr(self.server, "audit_checkpoint", None) is not None:
            self._proof(query)
            return
        if path == "/audit/checkpoint" \
                and getattr(self.server, "audit_checkpoint", None) is not None:
            # The endpoint takes no parameters: the snapshot is always
            # the one checkpoint file fixed at startup.
            self._checkpoint(query)
            return
        if path == "/acceptance" \
                and getattr(self.server, "acceptance_dir", None) is not None:
            self._acceptance(query)
            return
        if path == "/migration-batches" \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_batches", None) \
                is not None:
            self._migration_batches(query)
            return
        if path == "/migration-batches/events" \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_batches", None) \
                is not None:
            self._migration_batch_events(query)
            return
        if path == "/migration-consumers/status" \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_batches", None) \
                is not None \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_consumers", None) \
                is not None:
            self._migration_consumer_status(query)
            return
        if path == "/migration-consumers/dead-letters" \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_batches", None) \
                is not None \
                and getattr(self.server, "migration_consumers", None) \
                is not None:
            self._migration_consumer_dead_letters(query)
            return
        if path == "/completions" \
                and getattr(self.server, "completions_path", None) \
                is not None:
            self._completions(query)
            return
        self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found"})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - BaseHTTPRequestHandler contract
        path, _, query = self.path.partition("?")
        configured = getattr(self.server, "migration_batches", None) \
            is not None and getattr(self.server, "migration_consumers",
                                   None) is not None
        if path in _MIGRATION_CONSUMER_PATHS and configured:
            operation = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
            self._migration_consumer(operation, query)
            return
        self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found"})

    def _read_consumer_body(self, operation: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
        # One fixed JSON object per operation: exact field set, no
        # duplicates, non-boolean integer moments, no nulls beyond the
        # optional claim filters and no client-selected paths. Anything
        # else is a 400 and never reaches a ledger.
        allowed, required = {
            "claim": (_MIGRATION_CLAIM_FIELDS, _MIGRATION_CLAIM_REQUIRED),
            "pull": (_MIGRATION_PULL_FIELDS, _MIGRATION_PULL_REQUIRED),
            "ack": (_MIGRATION_ACK_FIELDS, _MIGRATION_ACK_FIELDS),
            "reject": (_MIGRATION_REJECT_FIELDS, _MIGRATION_REJECT_FIELDS),
        }[operation]

        def reject_duplicates(pairs):
            keys = [name for name, _value in pairs]
            if len(keys) != len(set(keys)):
                raise ValueError("duplicate JSON object member")
            return dict(pairs)

        def reject_constant(_token: str) -> float:
            # NaN/Infinity are never valid request literals.
            raise ValueError("non-finite JSON literal")

        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
            if length < 0 or length > _MIGRATION_MAX_BODY:
                raise ValueError("bad content length")
            raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
            body = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"),
                             parse_constant=reject_constant,
                             object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicates)
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
            return None
        if not isinstance(body, dict) \
                or not required.issubset(body) \
                or not set(body).issubset(allowed):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
            return None
        for name in ("consumer", "owner"):
            value = body[name]
            if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
        now = body["now"]
        if not isinstance(now, int) or isinstance(now, bool) or now < 0:
            self._bad_request()
            return None
        if operation == "claim":
            lease = body["lease"]
            if not isinstance(lease, int) or isinstance(lease, bool) \
                    or lease < 1:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
            for name in ("key", "job_id"):
                if name in body and body[name] is not None \
                        and (not isinstance(body[name], str)
                             or not body[name]):
                    self._bad_request()
                    return None
            if not isinstance(body["idem"], str) or not body["idem"]:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
        elif operation == "ack":
            position = body["position"]
            if not isinstance(position, int) or isinstance(position, bool) \
                    or position < 0:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
            if not isinstance(body["idem"], str) or not body["idem"]:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
        elif operation == "reject":
            position = body["position"]
            if not isinstance(position, int) or isinstance(position, bool) \
                    or position < 0:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
            # The content rule is a parameter validity check, enforced
            # here like position's range so an invalid reason answers
            # 400 before the subscription scope is read or the consumer
            # is looked up: surrounding whitespace is stripped and the
            # remainder must span 1..512 Unicode code points (code
            # points, not UTF-16 units or bytes).
            reason = body["reason"]
            if not isinstance(reason, str) \
                    or not 1 <= len(reason.strip()) <= 512:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
            if not isinstance(body["idem"], str) or not body["idem"]:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
        elif "limit" in body:
            limit = body["limit"]
            if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) \
                    or not 1 <= limit <= _MAX_LIMIT:
                self._bad_request()
                return None
        return body

    def _bad_request(self) -> None:
        self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})

    def _migration_consumer(self, operation: str, query: str) -> None:
        coordination = getattr(self.server, "migration_batches")
        consumers = getattr(self.server, "migration_consumers")
        authorized, record = self._authorize()
        if not authorized:
            return
        # No endpoint takes a query string; checked after identity like
        # the other parameter validations, before the body and any file.
        if query:
            self._bad_request()
            return
        body = self._read_consumer_body(operation)
        if body is None:
            return
        consumer = body["consumer"]
        owner = body["owner"]
        now = body["now"]

        # Scope follows body validation and precedes the coordination
        # stream read. The operation and stage axes need no file and are
        # decided first. A claim carries the batch key in the request; a
        # pull or ack never names it, so the key axis reads the
        # consumer's persisted fixed subscription from this endpoint's
        # own control ledger (at the same stage the auth configuration
        # is re-read). The data-plane coordination and business ledgers
        # open only after the scope is allowed.
        if record is not None and (record.ops is not None
                                   or record.stages is not None):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
            return
        batch_key: str | None
        if operation == "claim":
            batch_key = body.get("key")
        elif record is not None and record.keys is None:
            batch_key = None
        else:
            try:
                subscription = migration_batch.consumer_subscription(
                    coordination, consumers, consumer)
            except KeyError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                           {"error": "migration_consumer_not_found"})
                return
            except migration_batch.ConsumerLedgerInvalid:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_invalid"})
                return
            except FileNotFoundError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
                return
            except OSError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_unavailable"})
                return
            batch_key = subscription["key"]
        if record is not None and record.keys is not None:
            allowed = batch_key is not None and batch_key in record.keys
            if not allowed:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN,
                           {"error": "forbidden"})
                return

        kwargs: dict[str, object] = {}
        if operation == "claim":
            if "key" in body:
                kwargs["key"] = body["key"]
            if "job_id" in body:
                kwargs["job_id"] = body["job_id"]
            kwargs["lease"] = body["lease"]
            kwargs["idem"] = body["idem"]
        elif operation == "ack":
            kwargs["position"] = body["position"]
            kwargs["idem"] = body["idem"]
        elif operation == "reject":
            kwargs["position"] = body["position"]
            kwargs["reason"] = body["reason"]
            kwargs["idem"] = body["idem"]
        elif "limit" in body:
            kwargs["limit"] = body["limit"]

        try:
            payload = migration_batch.consume_response(
                coordination, consumers, operation, consumer, owner, now,
                **kwargs)
        except KeyError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumer_not_found"})
        except (migration_batch.ConsumerOwnershipError,
                migration_batch.ConsumerLeaseExpired):
            # A live lease owned by another caller, or an expired lease
            # the caller no longer holds: an ownership conflict. These
            # dedicated subclasses keep a filesystem PermissionError
            # from the commit falling through as 503 instead of 409.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_consumer_ownership"})
        except LookupError:
            # The confirmed cursor points at an event the current stream
            # truncated, rewrote or reused: a stream regression.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_consumer_checkpoint"})
        except migration_batch.CoordinationLedgerInvalid:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_batches_invalid"})
        except migration_batch.ConsumerLedgerInvalid:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_invalid"})
        except migration_batch.CoordinationLedgerMissing:
            # The fixed coordination ledger itself is missing; it keeps
            # the read-only endpoint's 404 and never leaks its path.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_batches_not_found"})
        except migration_batch.ConsumersLedgerMissing:
            # The configured consumer ledger parent does not exist.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
        except FileNotFoundError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
        except ValueError:
            # A changed idempotent request, a backward or past-tail ack,
            # a non-matching ack target or any other invalid argument.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
        except OSError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_unavailable"})
        else:
            self._bytes(HTTPStatus.OK, payload)

    def _migration_consumer_status(self, query: str) -> None:
        # Read-only consumer status: identity, parameters, the
        # persisted subscription read for scope, and only then the
        # coordination/business snapshot -- a failure at one stage
        # never opens a later stage's files.
        coordination = getattr(self.server, "migration_batches")
        consumers = getattr(self.server, "migration_consumers")
        authorized, record = self._authorize()
        if not authorized:
            return
        try:
            params = _parse_migration_consumer_status_params(query)
        except ValueError:
            self._bad_request()
            return
        consumer = params["consumer"]
        now = int(params["now"])

        # Operation- and stage-scoped tokens can never read a consumer;
        # an unrestricted key scope reads any subscription. A key-scoped
        # token reads the consumer's fixed subscription from the
        # consumer ledger at the scope stage, exactly like a pull or
        # ack: only a fixed-batch subscription naming an allowed batch
        # passes, while a cross-batch or job-only range needs all three
        # scopes unrestricted. The data-plane coordination and business
        # ledgers open only after the scope is allowed.
        if record is not None and (record.ops is not None
                                   or record.stages is not None):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
            return
        if record is not None and record.keys is not None:
            try:
                subscription = migration_batch.consumer_subscription(
                    coordination, consumers, consumer)
            except KeyError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                           {"error": "migration_consumer_not_found"})
                return
            except migration_batch.ConsumerLedgerInvalid:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_invalid"})
                return
            except FileNotFoundError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
                return
            except OSError:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                           {"error": "migration_consumers_unavailable"})
                return
            batch_key = subscription["key"]
            if batch_key is None or batch_key not in record.keys:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
                return

        try:
            payload = migration_batch.consumer_status_response(
                coordination, consumers, consumer, now)
        except KeyError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumer_not_found"})
        except LookupError:
            # The confirmed cursor points at an event the current
            # stream truncated, rewrote or reused: a stream regression.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_consumer_checkpoint"})
        except migration_batch.CoordinationLedgerInvalid:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_batches_invalid"})
        except migration_batch.ConsumerLedgerInvalid:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_invalid"})
        except migration_batch.CoordinationLedgerMissing:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_batches_not_found"})
        except migration_batch.ConsumersLedgerMissing:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
        except FileNotFoundError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_not_found"})
        except ValueError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
        except OSError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                       {"error": "migration_consumers_unavailable"})
        else:
            self._bytes(HTTPStatus.OK, payload)

    def _authorize(self) -> tuple[bool, auth.Record | None]:
        # Authorization comes first: an unauthorized request learns nothing
        # about the query, the configured paths or the journal's state.
        # Returns (True, record) once the caller may proceed; on failure
        # the error response is already sent and the result is (False, _).
        tokens = self.headers.get_all("X-Audit-Token")
        if tokens is None or len(tokens) != 1 or not tokens[0].strip():
            self._json(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, {"error": "unauthorized"})
            return False, None

        record: auth.Record | None = None
        auth_path = getattr(self.server, "audit_auth", None)
        if auth_path is not None:
            # Multi-token mode: the configuration is re-read on every
            # request, so a same-directory atomic replacement rotates
            # tokens without a restart and each request sees either the
            # complete old or the complete new configuration. A file
            # that can no longer be read or validated makes
            # authorization itself unavailable.
            try:
                records = auth.load(auth_path)
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                           {"error": "auth_unavailable"})
                return False, None
            # An unknown digest and a token past its grace cutoff are
            # indistinguishable: both are a plain 403.
            record = auth.identify(records, tokens[0])
            if record is None:
                self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
                return False, None
        else:
            expected = getattr(self.server, "audit_token").encode("utf-8")
            if not hmac.compare_digest(tokens[0].encode("utf-8"), expected):
                self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
                return False, None
        return True, record

    def _audit(self, query: str) -> None:
        authorized, record = self._authorize()
        if not authorized:
            return

        try:
            params = _parse_audit_params(query)
        except ValueError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
            return

        # Scope checks follow parameter validation and precede any access
        # to the journal: a forbidden request never opens the audit file
        # and never learns about records, token names or the configuration.
        if record is not None and not auth.scope_allows(record, params):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
            return

        kwargs: dict[str, object] = {}
        for name in ("cursor", "op", "stage", "key"):
            if name in params:
                kwargs[name] = params[name]
        if "limit" in params:
            kwargs["limit"] = int(params["limit"])

        try:
            result = audit.search(getattr(self.server, "audit_path"), **kwargs)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            # Never leak the configured path or the system message.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "audit_not_found"})
        except ValueError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "audit_invalid"})
        except OSError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                       {"error": "audit_unavailable"})
        else:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)

    def _proof(self, query: str) -> None:
        authorized, record = self._authorize()
        if not authorized:
            return

        try:
            params = _parse_proof_params(query)
        except ValueError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid_request"})
            return

        # Same order as the plain audit query: scopes are checked against
        # the validated filters before any file is opened.
        if record is not None and not auth.scope_allows(record, params):
            self._json(HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN, {"error": "forbidden"})
            return

        kwargs: dict[str, object] = {}
        for name in ("cursor", "op", "stage", "key"):
            if name in params:
                kwargs[name] = params[name]
        if "limit" in params:
            kwargs["limit"] = int(params["limit"])

        try:
            proof = audit_proof.export(
                getattr(self.server, "audit_path"),
                getattr(self.server, "audit_checkpoint"),
                params["generation"],
                final=params.get("final") == "true",
                **kwargs)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            # A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory; the
            # configured paths never leak into the response.
            self._json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "proof_not_found"})
        except ValueError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "proof_invalid"})
        except OSError:
            self._json(HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,

    def _raw(self, status: HTTPStatus, body: bytes, etag: str) -> None:
        # The snapshot bytes are served verbatim -- the original UTF-8
        # written by the exporter, with its field order intact -- and the
        # tag is the strong SHA-256 of those exact bytes.
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("ETag", f'"{etag}"')
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        if body:
            self.wfile.write(body)

    def _bytes(self, status: HTTPStatus, body: bytes) -> None:
        # Serve already-serialized compact UTF-8 JSON bytes verbatim, as
        # the read-only library builder formed them under its locks.
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        if body:
            self.wfile.write(body)

    def _json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: object) -> None:
        # Compact JSON with non-ASCII written through as direct UTF-8 and
        # no trailing newline, matching the persistent files' convention.
        body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False,
                          separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:
        return


def serve(host: str, port: int, audit_path: str | None = None,
          token: str | None = None, auth: str | None = None,
          checkpoint: str | None = None,
          acceptance: str | None = None,
          migration_batches: str | None = None,
          migration_consumers: str | None = None,
          completions: str | None = None) -> None:
    with ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), Handler) as server:
        server.audit_path = audit_path  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.audit_token = token  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.audit_auth = auth  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.audit_checkpoint = checkpoint  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.acceptance_dir = acceptance  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.migration_batches = migration_batches  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.migration_consumers = migration_consumers  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.completions_path = completions  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        server.serve_forever()

1	"""Authenticated ingestion of signed live signals.
2	
3	The :mod:`carbon_market.signals` ledger persists signal versions without
4	asking where they came from; this module adds the source-authenticated
5	write path. A source proves its identity and the request's integrity
6	with an HMAC-SHA256 envelope, and every accepted request is recorded in
7	its own receipt ledger.
8	
9	The envelope carries exactly five fields -- ``source``, ``key_id``,
10	``sequence``, ``signal`` and ``signature``. ``source`` and ``key_id``
11	are non-empty strings naming the sending source and the key it signed
12	with; ``sequence`` is a non-boolean positive integer; ``signal`` is a
13	signal object with the existing six fields
14	(``signals._SIGNAL_FIELDS``) and their existing validation; and
15	``signature`` is the lowercase hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 -- exactly 64
16	digits -- of the signing text.
17	
18	The signing text is the compact UTF-8 JSON array made, in order, of
19	``source``, ``key_id``, ``sequence`` and ``signal``; inside the signal
20	the six fields keep their fixed order and the ``mix`` keys are ordered
21	by Unicode code point. It therefore serializes independently of the
22	key order the envelope or signal dictionaries happened to arrive in.
23	
24	The trust file is one canonical compact JSON document. It maps each
25	source to exactly ``key_id`` (the unique key identifier that source may
26	sign with), ``key`` (the key as a non-empty even-length lowercase
27	hexadecimal string), ``regions`` (an array of distinct non-empty region
28	strings the source is authorized for) and ``valid_from`` and
29	``valid_until`` (non-boolean non-negative moments); the source may use
30	its key exactly when the signal's ``observed`` moment lies in the
31	closed interval between them. Like every other persisted document its
32	on-disk bytes must be the canonical compact form, and a non-canonical
33	file is rejected.
34	
35	Two identities decide admission. Each *source* accepts only strictly
36	increasing sequences -- a later request must carry a sequence greater
37	than every sequence already recorded for that source. The caller also
38	supplies an idempotency ``key`` for the ingest call itself: an exact
39	replay of the identical envelope under the same key returns the stored
40	receipt with ``False`` even once later sequences have been accepted,
41	while the same key carrying any changed envelope field is rejected. A
42	different key can never replay another key's sequence, because the
43	sequence is then not strictly increasing.
44	
45	A first request first persists a ``pending`` receipt, then publishes
46	the signal under an idempotency key derived deterministically from the
47	authenticated request, and finally settles the receipt as ``active``
48	and returns ``True``. An interrupted request resumes from its pending

50	active replay never rewrites a file.

232	                             ("valid_until", valid_until)):
233	            if not _is_plain_int(moment) or moment < 0:
234	                raise ValueError(f"trust {name} must be a non-boolean "
235	                                 "non-negative integer")
236	        if valid_until < valid_from:
237	            raise ValueError("trust valid_until must not be earlier than "
238	                             "valid_from")
239	
240	        key_ids.add(key_id)
241	        keys[source] = _TrustKey(
242	            key_id, bytes.fromhex(key_hex), frozenset(regions),
243	            valid_from, valid_until)
244	        plain[source] = {
245	            "key_id": key_id,
246	            "key": key_hex,
247	            "regions": plain_regions,
248	            "valid_from": valid_from,
249	            "valid_until": valid_until,
250	        }
251	    return keys, plain
252	
253	
254	def _serialize_trust(plain: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
255	    payload = {source: plain[source] for source in sorted(plain)}
256	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
257	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
258	    return text.encode("utf-8")
259	
260	
261	def _load_trust(realpath: str) -> dict[str, _TrustKey]:
262	    with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
263	        raw = handle.read()
264	    try:
265	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
266	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
267	        raise ValueError(f"trust file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") \
268	            from exc
269	    try:
270	        data = finite_loads(text)
271	    except ValueError as exc:
272	        raise ValueError(f"trust file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") \
273	            from exc
274	    keys, plain = _validate_trust(data)
275	    if raw != _serialize_trust(plain):
276	        raise ValueError(
277	            f"trust file {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
278	    return keys

281	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
282	# Envelope and signing text
283	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
284	
285	def _canonical_signal(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
286	    # The signal's six fields in their fixed order, mix ordered by code
287	    # point; values are already normalized by signals._normalize_signal.
288	    return {
289	        "region": signal["region"],
290	        "observed": signal["observed"],
291	        "expires": signal["expires"],
292	        "mix": {source: signal["mix"][source]
293	                for source in sorted(signal["mix"])},
294	        "unit_cost": signal["unit_cost"],
295	        "carbon_intensity": signal["carbon_intensity"],
296	    }
297	
298	
299	def _signing_bytes(source: str, key_id: str, sequence: int,
300	                   signal: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
301	    payload = [source, key_id, sequence, _canonical_signal(signal)]
302	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
303	                      allow_nan=False)
304	    return text.encode("utf-8")
305	
306	
307	def _is_signature(raw: object) -> bool:
308	    return isinstance(raw, str) and len(raw) == 64 \
309	        and all(char in _HEX_DIGITS for char in raw)
310	
311	
312	def _validate_envelope(envelope: object) -> tuple[str, str, int,
313	                                                  dict[str, Any], str]:
314	    if not isinstance(envelope, dict) \
315	            or set(envelope.keys()) != set(_ENVELOPE_FIELDS):
316	        raise ValueError("envelope must be an object with exactly source, "
317	                         "key_id, sequence, signal and signature")
318	    source = envelope["source"]
319	    key_id = envelope["key_id"]
320	    sequence = envelope["sequence"]
321	    signature = envelope["signature"]
322	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
323	        raise ValueError("envelope source must be a non-empty string")
324	    if not isinstance(key_id, str) or not key_id:
325	        raise ValueError("envelope key_id must be a non-empty string")
326	    if not _is_plain_int(sequence) or sequence < 1:
327	        raise ValueError("envelope sequence must be a non-boolean positive "
328	                         "integer")
329	    if not _is_signature(signature):
330	        raise ValueError("envelope signature must be 64 lowercase "
331	                         "hexadecimal digits")
332	    # The signal keeps the existing six fields and their full validation.
333	    normalized = _signals._normalize_signal(envelope["signal"])
334	    return source, key_id, sequence, normalized, signature
335	
336	
337	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
338	# Receipt ledger
339	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
340	
341	def _validate_receipt(raw: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
342	    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or list(raw.keys()) != list(_RECEIPT_FIELDS):
343	        raise ValueError("receipts must be objects with keys source, "
344	                         "key_id, sequence, region, signal_version, "
345	                         "signature and state, in that order")
346	    source = raw["source"]
347	    key_id = raw["key_id"]
348	    sequence = raw["sequence"]
349	    region = raw["region"]
350	    signal_version = raw["signal_version"]
351	    signature = raw["signature"]
352	    state = raw["state"]
353	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
354	        raise ValueError("receipt source must be a non-empty string")
355	    if not isinstance(key_id, str) or not key_id:
356	        raise ValueError("receipt key_id must be a non-empty string")
357	    if not _is_plain_int(sequence) or sequence < 1:
358	        raise ValueError("receipt sequence must be a positive integer")
359	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
360	        raise ValueError("receipt region must be a non-empty string")
361	    # An active receipt froze a published version; a pending receipt was
362	    # written before the signal was published and carries 0.
363	    if not _is_plain_int(signal_version) or signal_version < 0 \
364	            or (state == "active") != (signal_version >= 1):
365	        raise ValueError("receipt signal_version must be 0 while pending "
366	                         "and a positive integer once active")
367	    if not _is_signature(signature):
368	        raise ValueError("receipt signature must be 64 lowercase "
369	                         "hexadecimal digits")
370	    if state not in _STATES:
371	        raise ValueError("receipt state must be pending or active")
372	    return {field: raw[field] for field in _RECEIPT_FIELDS}
373	
374	
375	def _validate_ledger(data: object) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
376	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
377	        raise ValueError("receipt ledger root must be an object with keys "
378	                         "version and receipts, in that order")
379	    version = data["version"]
380	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
381	        raise ValueError("unsupported receipt ledger version")
382	    receipts_raw = data["receipts"]
383	    if not isinstance(receipts_raw, dict):
384	        raise ValueError("receipt ledger receipts must be an object")
385	    keys = list(receipts_raw)
386	    if keys != sorted(keys):
387	        raise ValueError("receipt ledger keys must be ordered by code "
388	                         "point")
389	    receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
390	    for ledger_key in keys:
391	        if not isinstance(ledger_key, str) or not ledger_key:
392	            raise ValueError("receipt ledger keys must be non-empty "
393	                             "strings")
394	        receipts[ledger_key] = _validate_receipt(receipts_raw[ledger_key])
395	    return receipts
396	
397	
398	def _serialize(receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> bytes:
399	    payload = {
400	        "version": _VERSION,
401	        "receipts": {key: receipts[key] for key in sorted(receipts)},
402	    }
403	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
404	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
405	    return text.encode("utf-8")
406	
407	
408	def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
409	                                       bytes | None]:
410	    try:
411	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
412	            raw = handle.read()
413	    except FileNotFoundError:
414	        return {}, None
415	    try:
416	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
417	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
418	        raise ValueError(
419	            f"receipt ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
420	    try:
421	        data = finite_loads(text)
422	    except ValueError as exc:
423	        raise ValueError(
424	            f"receipt ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
425	    receipts = _validate_ledger(data)
426	    if raw != _serialize(receipts):
427	        raise ValueError(
428	            f"receipt ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
429	    return receipts, raw
430	
431	
432	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
433	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
434	    try:
435	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
436	    finally:
437	        os.close(dir_fd)
438	
439	
440	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
441	                   first: BaseException) -> None:
442	    # Restore the exact pre-stage bytes while the exclusive lock is held
443	    # so an unsuccessful stage leaves a complete earlier (or resumable
444	    # pending) state, never a torn write.
445	    try:
446	        if old_bytes is None:
447	            try:
448	                os.unlink(realpath)
449	            except FileNotFoundError:
450	                pass
451	        else:
452	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
453	                dir=directory, prefix=".ingest-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
454	            try:
455	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
456	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
457	                    handle.flush()
458	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
459	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
460	            except BaseException:
461	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
462	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
463	                raise
464	        _fsync_directory(directory)
465	    except OSError as recovery:
466	        raise recovery from first
467	
468	
469	def _commit_file(realpath: str, receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
470	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> bytes:
471	    # One durable commit per stage; returns the bytes just committed,
472	    # which become the rollback target for the following stage.
473	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
474	    payload = _serialize(receipts)
475	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
476	        dir=directory, prefix=".ingest-", suffix=".tmp")
477	    try:
478	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
479	            handle.write(payload)
480	            handle.flush()
481	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
482	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
483	    except BaseException:
484	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
485	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
486	        raise
487	    try:
488	        _fsync_directory(directory)
489	    except BaseException as first:
490	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
491	        raise
492	    return payload
493	
494	
495	def _request_key(source: str, key_id: str, sequence: int) -> str:
496	    # Stable textual form of the authenticated triple, used to derive
497	    # the signal ledger's idempotency key. The strings are JSON-quoted
498	    # so no separator can be spoofed; the sequence is a plain integer.
499	    return (json.dumps(source, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
500	            + " " + json.dumps(key_id, ensure_ascii=False,
501	                                    separators=(",", ":"))
502	            + " " + str(sequence))
503	
504	
505	def _idem_key(source: str, key_id: str, sequence: int,
506	              signature: str) -> str:
507	    # Deterministically derived from the whole authenticated request:
508	    # the source, the key it signed with, its sequence and the exact
509	    # signature. An identical request derives the same key and replays
510	    # through signals' own idempotency; a changed field derives another.
511	    digest = hashlib.sha256(
512	        _request_key(source, key_id, sequence).encode("utf-8")
513	        + b" " + signature.encode("ascii")).hexdigest()
514	    return _IDEM_PREFIX + digest
515	
516	
517	def _public_receipt(receipt: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
518	    # Fixed field order, no key material.
519	    return {field: receipt[field] for field in _RECEIPT_FIELDS}
520	
521	
522	def _same_envelope(existing: dict[str, Any], source: str, key_id: str,
523	                   sequence: int, region: str, signature: str) -> bool:
524	    return (existing["source"] == source
525	            and existing["key_id"] == key_id
526	            and existing["sequence"] == sequence
527	            and existing["region"] == region
528	            and existing["signature"] == signature)
529	
530	
531	def _highest_sequence(receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
532	                      source: str) -> int | None:
533	    highest: int | None = None
534	    for receipt in receipts.values():
535	        if receipt["source"] == source and (
536	                highest is None or receipt["sequence"] > highest):
537	            highest = receipt["sequence"]
538	    return highest
539	
540	
541	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
542	# Entry point
543	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
544	
545	def ingest(signals: str, trust: str, ledger: str, envelope: dict[str, Any],
546	           key: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
547	    """Authenticate and persist one signed signal envelope.
548	
549	    ``signals`` is the existing signal ledger path (its format and the
550	    :func:`signals.publish`/:func:`signals.get` semantics are
551	    unchanged), ``trust`` the canonical trust file and ``ledger`` the
552	    receipt ledger written by this module. The three paths and ``key``
553	    must be non-empty strings, the paths resolving to distinct real
554	    locations. ``key`` is the idempotency key of the ingest call: the
555	    receipt ledger is keyed by it, although the receipt itself never
556	    stores it.
557	
558	    The envelope is validated and its HMAC checked against the trusted
559	    key for its source; an unknown source or ``key_id`` or a mismatched
560	    signature raises :class:`PermissionError`. The key must be valid at
561	    the signal's ``observed`` moment and the region must be authorized,
562	    else :class:`ValueError`. Sequences per source must be strictly
563	    increasing. Under an existing ``key`` an exact replay of the
564	    identical envelope returns the stored receipt with ``False`` even
565	    after later sequences were accepted and writes nothing; the same
566	    ``key`` carrying any changed field raises :class:`ValueError`
567	    (conflicting idempotency key), as does a derived signal publication
568	    key already bound to a different signal.
569	
570	    A first request persists a ``pending`` receipt, publishes the signal
571	    under the derived idempotency key and then settles the receipt as
572	    ``active``; it returns ``(receipt, True)``. Retrying an interrupted
573	    request resumes from its pending receipt and never creates a second
574	    signal version. A missing trust file or a missing parent directory
575	    of either written file raises :class:`FileNotFoundError`;
576	    non-canonical trust or receipt files or illegal arguments raise
577	    :class:`ValueError`; other locking or read/write failures raise
578	    :class:`OSError`.
579	    """
580	    for value in (signals, trust, ledger, key):
581	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
582	            raise ValueError("signals, trust, ledger paths and key must be "
583	                             "non-empty strings")
584	
585	    source, key_id, sequence, signal, signature = _validate_envelope(
586	        envelope)
587	    region = signal["region"]
588	
589	    trust_real = os.path.realpath(trust)
590	    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
591	    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signals)
592	    if len({trust_real, ledger_real, signal_real}) != 3:
593	        raise ValueError("signals, trust and ledger paths must be distinct "
594	                         "real paths")
595	
596	    publish_key = _idem_key(source, key_id, sequence, signature)
597	
598	    # The receipt ledger drives the transaction; serialize per ledger
599	    # path in-process as well as across processes.
600	    store = _get_store(ledger)
601	    with store.lock:
602	        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
603	            # Three files, one resolved-real-path lock order shared by
604	            # every caller: the two ledgers are written (exclusive), the
605	            # trust file is only read (shared).
606	            for locked, shared in sorted(
607	                    ((trust_real, True), (ledger_real, False),
608	                     (signal_real, False)), key=lambda item: item[0]):
609	                stack.enter_context(_file_lock(locked, shared=shared))
610	
611	            trusted = _load_trust(trust_real)
612	
613	            trusted_key = trusted.get(source)
614	            # Authentication failures do not reveal whether the source
615	            # or the key was unknown and carry no key material.
616	            if trusted_key is None or trusted_key.key_id != key_id:
617	                raise PermissionError("unknown signal source or key")
618	            expected = hmac.new(
619	                trusted_key.secret,
620	                _signing_bytes(source, key_id, sequence, signal),
621	                hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
622	            if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):
623	                raise PermissionError("envelope signature does not match")
624	
625	            # The signature proved the source; enforce the key's validity
626	            # window and regional authorization.
627	            observed = signal["observed"]
628	            if not trusted_key.valid_from <= observed \
629	                    <= trusted_key.valid_until:
630	                raise ValueError("signing key is not valid at the signal "
631	                                 "observation moment")
632	            if region not in trusted_key.regions:
633	                raise ValueError("signal region is not authorized for the "
634	                                 "source")
635	
636	            receipts, ledger_old = _load_file(ledger_real)
637	            history, idempotency, events, signal_old = \
638	                _signals._load_file(signal_real)
639	
640	            existing = receipts.get(key)
641	            if existing is not None:
642	                # Replay takes precedence over the sequence check: the
643	                # identical request returns its stored receipt even once
644	                # later sequences were accepted; any changed field under
645	                # the same idempotency key is a conflict.
646	                if not _same_envelope(existing, source, key_id, sequence,
647	                                      region, signature):
648	                    raise ValueError("ingest idempotency key was already "
649	                                     "used with a different request")
650	                if existing["state"] == "active":
651	                    _check_published(existing, publish_key, signal,
652	                                     idempotency, events, history)
653	                    return _public_receipt(existing), False
654	                # A pending receipt is resumed below.
655	                resume_from = existing
656	            else:
657	                # A source with an unresolved pending receipt is a gap in
658	                # its stream: block every new request for that source
659	                # until the pending key resumes. Otherwise a higher
660	                # sequence could publish first and strand the pending
661	                # signal behind a later observation, making its promised
662	                # recovery impossible.
663	                pending = [ledger_key for ledger_key, receipt in
664	                           receipts.items()
665	                           if receipt["source"] == source
666	                           and receipt["state"] == "pending"]
667	                if pending:
668	                    raise ValueError("source has an unresolved pending "
669	                                     "ingest that must be resumed first")
670	                # A different ingest key can never reuse a sequence the
671	                # source already recorded.
672	                highest = _highest_sequence(receipts, source)
673	                if highest is not None and sequence <= highest:
674	                    raise ValueError("sequence must be strictly increasing "
675	                                     "per source")
676	                # The derived publish key must not bind another signal in
677	                # the existing ledger. The underlying region observation
678	                # ordering is checked up front as well, so after the
679	                # pending receipt is written the publication can only
680	                # fail on a read/write fault and a retry resumes cleanly.
681	                bound_region = idempotency.get(publish_key)
682	                if bound_region is not None:
683	                    event = events[publish_key]
684	                    bound = history[bound_region][event["version"] - 1]
685	                    if {field: bound[field]
686	                            for field in _signals._SIGNAL_FIELDS} != signal:
687	                        raise ValueError("derived signal idempotency key "
688	                                         "conflicts with an existing "
689	                                         "binding")
690	                versions = history.get(region)
691	                if versions is not None \
692	                        and signal["observed"] <= versions[-1]["observed"]:
693	                    raise ValueError("signal observation must increase "
694	                                     "across versions")
695	                resume_from = None
696	
697	            return _adopt(
698	                resume_from, key, source, key_id, sequence, region,
699	                signature, ledger_real, receipts, ledger_old, signal_real,
700	                history, idempotency, events, signal_old, publish_key,
701	                signal)
702	
703	
704	def _check_published(
705	    existing: dict[str, Any], publish_key: str, signal: dict[str, Any],
706	    idempotency: dict[str, str], events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
707	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
708	) -> None:
709	    # An active receipt is only returned when the signal ledger still
710	    # holds the exact publication the receipt froze; an active replay
711	    # itself never writes a byte.
712	    bound_region = idempotency.get(publish_key)
713	    if bound_region is None:
714	        raise ValueError("receipt references a missing signal publication")
715	    event = events[publish_key]
716	    record = history[bound_region][event["version"] - 1]
717	    if record["version"] != existing["signal_version"] \
718	            or {field: record[field]
719	                for field in _signals._SIGNAL_FIELDS} != signal:
720	        raise ValueError("receipt no longer matches its published signal")
721	
722	
723	def _adopt(
724	    resume_from: dict[str, Any] | None, key: str,
725	    source: str, key_id: str, sequence: int, region: str, signature: str,
726	    ledger_real: str, receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
727	    ledger_old: bytes | None,
728	    signal_real: str,
729	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], idempotency: dict[str, str],
730	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], signal_old: bytes | None,
731	    publish_key: str, signal: dict[str, Any],
732	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
733	    if resume_from is None:
734	        # Stage 1: persist the pending receipt before the signal is
735	        # published, so an interruption leaves exactly this one
736	        # explainable, resumable stage.
737	        receipt: dict[str, Any] = {
738	            "source": source,
739	            "key_id": key_id,
740	            "sequence": sequence,
741	            "region": region,
742	            "signal_version": 0,
743	            "signature": signature,
744	            "state": "pending",
745	        }
746	        receipts[key] = receipt
747	        pending_bytes = _commit_file(ledger_real, receipts, ledger_old)
748	        stage3_target: bytes | None = pending_bytes
749	    else:
750	        # Resuming: the pending receipt survived the interruption; keep
751	        # it as the rollback target for the final commit.
752	        receipt = resume_from
753	        stage3_target = ledger_old
754	
755	    # Stage 2: publish the existing signal under the derived key. Either
756	    # this call creates the one version, or the pre-crash call already
757	    # did and the ledger replays it with False -- a resume never creates
758	    # a second version. If the publication itself faults, the pending
759	    # receipt stays on disk as the recoverable state and signals' own
760	    # commit restores the pre-call signal bytes, so retrying the same
761	    # request resumes cleanly.
762	    record, _created = _signals._publish_locked(
763	        signal_real, signal, publish_key, history, idempotency, events,
764	        signal_old)
765	    receipt["signal_version"] = record["version"]
766	    receipt["state"] = "active"
767	    _commit_file(ledger_real, receipts, stage3_target)
768	    return _public_receipt(receipt), True
